CausalChain: Exosomes can efficiently deliver miRNAs -> Synthetic enrichment of miR-128-3p in exosomes -> Uptake by oxaliplatin-resistant colorectal cancer cells -> miR-128-3p downregulates Bmi1 -> Reduction of Bmi1 leads to decreased MRP5 expression and reversal of EMT -> Reversal of EMT restores drug sensitivity.
Hypothesis: Engineering exosomes enriched with miR-128-3p can be used to reverse the EMT phenotype and enhance chemosensitivity in oxaliplatin-resistant colorectal cancer by targeting the Bmi1/MRP5 axis.
Abstract: We propose that exosome‐mediated delivery of synthetic miR‐128‐3p can reverse the epithelial–mesenchymal transition (EMT) and overcome chemoresistance in oxaliplatin‐resistant colorectal cancer. Elevated levels of miR‐128‐3p in exosomes taken up by tumor cells may suppress the expression of the oncogene Bmi1 that promotes EMT and upregulates drug efflux transporters such as MRP5. This process is expected to shift resistant cells to a more epithelial state, thereby increasing their sensitivity to chemotherapy. This therapeutic strategy may offer a novel means to overcome chemoresistance by targeting both the EMT regulatory network and drug efflux mechanisms.
